properties.title: Learning a patient world model for health system simulation in intensive care
properties.contribution_type: Primary method – new model + health system simulation

membership.reason: Time-conditioned patient world model (pWM) coupled to a discrete-event virtual ICU simulator to evaluate operational capacity, staffing, and dispatch policies.
membership.counting_boundary: Verified L1 temporal/autonomous patient world model coupled to exogenous discrete-event virtual ICU operational scenarios (WT_POPULATION, BP_OPERATIONAL).

properties.backbone: Dual-axis attention autoregressive patient world model (64 state vars, 25 event types) + discrete-event ICU simulator

properties.flow: Longitudinal EHR history -> frozen time-queryable pWM -> scenario-specific demand mappings -> discrete-event virtual ICU (beds, staff, queues)

properties.purpose: Health system simulation for ICU bed capacity, care dispatch, and post-ICU transfer policies.
properties.environment: Patient-level partitions of MIMIC-IV virtual ICU

assertions.rationale: Dual-axis attention over irregular state-event histories and continuous-valued forecast intervals.
Shared clinical patient state representation updated via recursive rollout.
Single frozen pWM serves multiple operational policy questions without rebuilding.
Retains history-dependent recovery contrasts missed by Markov models.
Time-queryable 14-day patient rollouts on a shared event clock.
Neural autoregressive pWM coupled to discrete-event operational queuing rules.
Repeated stochastic rollouts generating alternative individual futures and virtual cohorts.

Evaluated on held-out MIMIC-IV patients for both fixed-history clinical queries (Fig. 2, n=1,024: in-hospital mortality AUROC 0.937, 30-day ICU admission 0.881, recalibrated slope median 0.988) and 14-day multi-step autoregressive rollouts (Fig. 3, n=670, 10,720 trajectories: hourly five-state occupancy mean TVD 0.0388, integrated MAE 1.58% vs 1.53% Markov and 1.24% semi-Markov), with noted 14-day support-start incidence overestimation and attenuated circulatory initiation variance.
Couples frozen pWM rollouts to ICU operational dispatch, bed capacity, and transfer policy evaluation.
Health system simulation for hospital and ICU operational policy design.
14-day virtual cohort ICU occupancy, mortality AUROC 0.937, 30-day ICU admission 0.881.
Evaluates ICU bed capacity, care dispatch, and post-ICU transfer policies in virtual ICU.

evidence_fragments.content: Taking intensive care unit (ICU) operations as a working example, we train the model on MIMIC-IV, freeze it, and couple its time-queryable predictions to shared ICU calendars, resources, and queues via scenario-specific mappings, so that one model renders admission demand, care tasks, and discharge proposals across simulations evaluating ICU bed capacity, care dispatch, and post-ICU transfer capacity.

Trained on longitudinal EHRs, the neural autoregressive model represents irregular patient histories as sparse state–event sequences over a clinical vocabulary of 64 state variables and 25 event types (Fig. 1a). Dual-axis attention across clinical variables and elapsed time combines this context with continuous-valued forecast intervals, returning clinical predictions at the refresh times requested by the simulator.

Across tasks, AUROC reaches 0.937 for in-hospital mortality, 0.881 for 30-day ICU admission, 0.814 for 30-day ICU readmission, and 0.682 for 30-day hospital readmission, with precision–recall areas exceeding task prevalence across all six endpoints (Fig. 2a; Supplementary Fig. S1a).

We generate 16 recalibrated 14-day rollouts from the ICU-admission anchor of each of 670 held-out test patients (10,720 trajectories in total) and map trajectories to five states (no support, single-organ support, dual support, live discharge, and death).
With explicit observation and action interfaces, this environment could also support future evaluations of operational agents that prioritize care or allocate resources.

Second, like Markov and semi-Markov models fitted to observational records, the pWM learns conditional associations under historical care practices instead of causal effects [49–51]; rather than estimating how delayed care alters patient survival, our simulations quantify how capacity and dispatch policies shape admission access, queue waiting, and resource utilization under observed care patterns.

capability_assessments.rationale: Honestly downgraded from L4 to L1: the neural patient world model (pWM) implements persistent longitudinal EHR state (assertion:A11:019) and learned continuous-time autoregressive temporal dynamics (assertions 041, 042), quantitatively evaluated on held-out clinical endpoints and 14-day cohort rollouts (assertion:A11:053, L1). However, the pWM itself predicts trajectories under observed historical care practices without settable clinical/operational action conditioning or causal identification (p. 14), and no planner/optimizer/RL policy is implemented (Discussion p. 14 notes operational agents as future work; the outer discrete-event simulator evaluates fixed capacity and FIFO vs acute-first dispatch scenarios around frozen patient trajectories).

readiness_assessments.legacy_highest_label: R1 Single-center MIMIC-IV virtual ICU operational simulation

limitations: Single-center MIMIC-IV virtual ICU simulation; no prospective hospital deployment.

The frozen pWM is an autonomous observational trajectory predictor (L1) under historical care practices rather than an action-conditioned causal model or policy optimizer (L4); operational agents and causal delayed-care effects are explicitly deferred to future work (p. 14).

legacy_cells.B: Learning a patient world model for health system simulation in intensive care
legacy_cells.S: Can a single frozen patient-dynamics model support ICU admission, care-delivery, and discharge simulations under changing operational scenarios while retaining history-dependent patient differences?
legacy_cells.T: MIMIC-IV v3.1 hospital and ICU records (2008–2022); 364,627 patients and 94,444 ICU stays were processed.
legacy_cells.V: Compare ICU bed capacity, care-task dispatch, and downstream transfer-capacity scenarios to assess admission access, queues, and bed use.
legacy_cells.AI: Longitudinal EHR: discretized physiological/state measurements, medication and diagnosis/procedure labels, and clinical event records (including organ-support events).
legacy_cells.AJ: Six-layer Transformer encoder with 12 attention heads; variable-axis and causal time-axis attention plus a cross-slot query mixer.
legacy_cells.AN: Missing measurements remain unrecorded in the sparse EHR grid; no imputation is described.
legacy_cells.AS: 64 state variables and 25 event types; state measurements discretized into ten quantile bins.
legacy_cells.BL: Positive continuous-valued forecast interval Δ; timestamps rounded to seconds; simulator refresh default is 1 h; cohort rollouts span 14 days.
legacy_cells.BN: Organ-support rollout rules: start only if support is inactive; change or stop only if active; live discharge and death are absorbing projection states.
legacy_cells.BP: At most 1,536 time columns and 3,072 grid entries per example.
legacy_cells.BS: Future discretized clinical-state distributions, event intensities/occurrences, and conditional event-label distributions.
legacy_cells.BT: State-bin, event-intensity, conditional event-label, and target-before-stop endpoint readouts.
legacy_cells.BV: Next-time loss = ten-bin state cross-entropy + event loss + event-label cross-entropy; total loss adds αendpoint=0.10 times target-before-stop endpoint negative log-likelihood.
legacy_cells.CD: 14 days for reported autoregressive cohort rollouts.
legacy_cells.CG: 16 recalibrated 14-day rollouts per each of 670 held-out test patients (10,720 trajectories).
legacy_cells.CR: Calibration slopes across 24 binary task–horizon queries; median recalibrated slope 0.988 (IQR 0.885–1.051); nominal 80% state-interval coverage improved from 65.5% to 81.4% at 72 h.
legacy_cells.DQ: 364,627 patients and 94,444 ICU stays processed; 80% of patients assigned to model training, with remaining patients split between validation and held-out test.
legacy_cells.DR: One institution: Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center.
legacy_cells.DY: 14-day rollout: restricted mean ICU stay 2.923 days vs 2.800 observed; hourly five-state occupancy mean total-variation distance 0.0388 and Jensen–Shannon divergence 0.0044. At 14 days, support-start incidence was overestimated (respiratory 44.2% vs 29.7%; circulatory 42.7% vs 27.3%).
legacy_cells.DZ: Hourly five-state occupancy: mean total-variation distance 0.0388 and Jensen–Shannon divergence 0.0044; 99.8% of individual 14-day trajectories unique across repeated samples.
legacy_cells.EB: Operational-control sensitivity: acute-first dispatch reduced low-staffing acute queue burden by 13.41 h/patient for generated trajectories; increasing transfer slots shortened exit delays; capacity changes produced the expected directional operational responses.
legacy_cells.ED: Observed-trajectory replay: generated courses reproduced acute-first dispatch reductions closely (generated vs observed: 15.76 vs 14.99, 8.41 vs 7.88, and 1.68 vs 1.93 h/patient at low, middle, and high staffing).
legacy_cells.EI: Task-fitted Markov and semi-Markov comparators; 14-day hourly five-state occupancy integrated MAE was 1.58% (neural), 1.53% (Markov), and 1.24% (semi-Markov).
legacy_cells.EL: Reported rollout biases: respiratory and circulatory support-start incidence overestimated; dual-support occupancy lower (0.63% vs 1.16% of patient-hours); explicit-stop respiratory episodes shorter (20.6 vs 38.7 h); circulatory-start heterogeneity attenuated (variance log-ratio −1.31).
legacy_cells.EO: MIMIC-IV is de-identified; access requires credentialing, required research training, and a signed data-use agreement.
legacy_cells.ER: Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center IRB approves database creation and sharing and waives informed consent.
legacy_cells.FB: Sparse state–event representation over a shared vocabulary: 64 state variables, 25 event types, ten quantile bins for continuous state measurements, categorical event labels, and irregular timestamps.
legacy_cells.FL: Sparse longitudinal EHR state/event records are embedded and processed by a dual-axis Transformer; state-bin, event-intensity, and event-label distributions are autoregressively sampled and appended to patient history; scenario-specific mappings pass patient outputs into a discrete-event ICU simulator with shared beds, staff, queues, and configurable operational rules. No optimizer or learned planner is described.
legacy_cells.FM: Authors introduce a time-queryable patient world model trained on longitudinal EHRs and couple its frozen dynamics through scenario-specific mappings to ICU discrete-event operations, reusing one patient model across admission, care-delivery, and discharge simulations.
legacy_cells.FN: The pWM achieved in-hospital mortality AUROC 0.937 and median recalibrated calibration slope 0.988; simulated 14-day occupancy had mean TV distance 0.0388; in matched histories it reproduced a 24-h recovery contrast of −6.40 pp vs −6.68 pp observed; generated trajectories closely reproduced observed replay dispatch effects.
legacy_cells.FO: MIMIC-IV lacks empirical queue logs and staff schedules, so arrival streams, service durations, and capacities are scenario specifications; absolute waiting-time prediction or cross-hospital deployment requires workflow-data calibration and external validation. The pWM learns conditional associations under historical care, not causal effects.
legacy_cells.FP: Authors state that the environment could support future evaluation of operational agents that prioritize care or allocate resources, and that deployment as a digital twin would need live operational streams and local validation.
legacy_cells.FQ: Existing compact health-system transitions are tailored to single policy questions and can omit history-dependent dynamics; learned patient models had not been coupled to shared-clock resource demand mappings for health-system simulation.
legacy_cells.FR: Evidence is retrospective and internal to MIMIC-IV plus simulated operational scenarios. The reported policy effects concern capacities and dispatch under specified simulator rules, not identified causal physiological treatment effects; there is no external hospital validation, prospective evaluation, or deployed workflow evidence.
legacy_cells.FS: Reviewer mapping: M3 Belief-state service; M5 Dynamics adapter; M6 Rollout service; M7 Outcome & causal layer
legacy_cells.FT: Reviewer lesson: Expose future-state forecasts through a time-aware dynamics interface and validate error versus horizon; treatment actions need separate evidence before intervention simulation.
legacy_cells.FX: PDF pages 1–35: title/abstract (p. 1); introduction (pp. 2–3); Results and all main figures (pp. 4–14); Methods and all methodological figures (pp. 15–24); discussion/limitations (pp. 13–14); supplementary figures/results (pp. 30–35). The extracted PDF text was read through its final page; no unreadable table was encountered. | Codex audit: title/byline, abstract/conclusion, targeted methods/results and cross-check of prior quotations against extracted full text. This is a targeted audit, not an independent re-extraction of every negative/unreported field.
legacy_cells.FZ: A:I left unchanged. No causal treatment-effect identification is demonstrated; capacity and dispatch scenario comparisons do not establish physiological treatment counterfactuals. Readiness is retrospective internal validation (R2), separate from demonstrated L1 temporal prediction. The supplied rubric references KB §19.1 and §20 taxonomies, but those reference definitions were not among the declared inputs; FS and FU are therefore omitted rather than mapped speculatively. Evidence QA: 76/83 populated fields had a <=25-word quotation matching extracted PDF text (91.6%). Confidence is conservative; review this row where exact quote checks were incomplete. Compounding-error evidence (CF): Yes — distributional drift is quantified over generated-event prefixes up to 256 events; after recalibration, event-frequency TV and transition JS increase by 0.0379 and 0.0238 per cap doubling. Codex audit: 82 prior populated fields have a located source quotation; 1 have quotations not located by normalized text matching. Unlocated quotations are review flags, not proof that the value is false. Companion evidence audit lists affected columns. Reviewer FS/FT/FU mappings are synthesis.
